newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian airlines Orient-Avia, East Line Air merge.
newsitem.headline: Russian airlines Orient-Avia, East Line Air merge.

text.p: Private Russian airlines Orient-Avia and East Line Air announced on Friday they had merged to create a new airline, East Line Aviation.

Amiran Kurtanidze, chief executive of the new company, told Reuters the new carrier, to be based at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport, would be a serious competitor to leading airlines like Aeroflot and Transaero.
"We have merged our aircraft fleet and ground facilities to set up an aviation company with huge potential," he said. "We will challenge the market, especially to South East Asian destinations."
The new airline has a fleet of 46 cargo planes and and five passengers jets from East Line Air, and five Orient-Avia passenger planes.
"We plan initially to develop air cargo operations, but passenger services will later became a priority because Russia has a very promising market for passenger services," Kurtanidze said.
AO Orient-Avia, set up in 1994, carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996, up from 95,800 passengers and 860 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1995.

It operates regular flights between Moscow and Vladivostok and Petropalovsk-Kamchatsky in the Russian Far East and won permission this year from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration to fly between Russia and the United States.

AO East Line Air was established in 1995 as a cargo carrier. It carried 110,000 tonne of cargo last year, making 3,000 charters flights to 26 destinations, including Russia, China, India, Italy, Turkey, South Korea and United Arab Emirates.
The company annual turnover was $1 billion in 1996.
